Creation request payload for tagging a post with a board tag.

Requires both post_id (uuid) and tag_id (uuid). Business rules enforce existence and uniqueness constraints.

Source: discussionboard_post_tags Prisma table.

IDiscussionboardPostTag.IUpdate.description:
Update object for modifying post-tag assignment.

Rarely used; primarily for admin corrections or audits. Both fields optional and restricted per business/audit logic.

Source: discussionboard_post_tags Prisma model.

IDiscussionboardComment.IRequest.description:
Request object for searching, filtering, and paginating comments in the discussion board.

Includes filtering by post, author/member, parent (for threaded comments), creation time range, and paging control. Directly used in PATCH /discussionboard/comments.

IPageIDiscussionboardComment.description:
Paginated container for comments. Used to encapsulate comment result sets along with paging state.

Implements platform-wide IPage<T> interface, using IDiscussionboardComment.ISummary objects per item.

IDiscussionboardComment.description:
A complete discussion board comment entity, including threading info, author, timestamps, and deletion status.

Each object corresponds to a row in discussionboard_comments. Reference for display, moderation, deep audit review.

IDiscussionboardComment.ICreate.description:
Creation request payload for a new discussion board comment.

All fields required for a new top-level or reply comment, except parent_id (which is nullable for top-level).

IDiscussionboardComment.IUpdate.description:
Update object for editing comment body or deletion flag/restore. Used for UI comment editing, moderation removal, or restoring soft-deleted content.

Links to discussionboard_comments schema. Edits are restricted by edit window and permissions.

IDiscussionboardCommentEditHistory.IRequ.description:
Request filter object for listing/searching comment edit history entries.

Includes filtering by comment, editor, edited time range, and pagination. Pattern follows IPage<ICommentEditHistory> structure. Links to discussionboard_comment_edit_histories schema.

IPage.IPagination.description:
Metadata for paginated API responses. Indicates current page, per-page limit, total records, and total page count.

Standard IPage.IPagination for all pageable resources. Referenced by container types such as IPageIDiscussionboardPostTag, IPageIDiscussionboardComment, etc.

IDiscussionboardPostTag.ISummary.description: Summary properties for a post-tag association.

IDiscussionboardComment.ISummary.description: Summary properties for a comment, for use in paginated listings or list views.

IdiscussionboardBoards.ISummary.description: Summary view for a discussion board entity, used in paginated list results or quick-select UI panes. Contains essential detail for identification, navigation, and filtering.

IdiscussionboardBoardTags.ISummary.description: Summary record for a board tag entity, suitable for paginated tag lists and tag search result UIs. Contains minimal display information: tag label, board reference, and UUID.

operations.specification: List or search all channels in the discussion board system. Returns channels with pagination and filtering according to request parameters. Associated with the 'discussionboard_channels' Prisma table.
operations.description: This operation retrieves a paginated list of channels, allowing optional filters like visibility, name search, creation dates, and more as described in the discussionboard_channels schema and requirements document. Permissions may restrict some results for non-admin roles. The API incorporates sorting and advanced search, and will be used by admins, moderators, and members to discover channels. Error responses will provide validation, permission, and query failure details. Pagination uses standard page/size parameters, enabling large-scale enumeration without performance penalty.
operations.summary: List and search all channels in the discussion board (discussionboard_channels table).

requestBody.description: Filter, search, and pagination settings for retrieving channels.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of channels with summary info per channel.

operations.specification: Get details for a specific discussion board channel by unique id. Associated with 'discussionboard_channels' Prisma table.
operations.description: This operation retrieves the complete information for a single channel entity, including name, description, timestamps, and any visibility or deletion status. The id path parameter corresponds to the primary UUID key of the discussionboard_channels Prisma table. Used for displaying channel detail views in user interfaces, and for management tasks by admins or moderators. Permission rules restrict access to hidden or soft-deleted channels for some roles. Errors will be returned for invalid ids or insufficient permissions.
operations.summary: Get details of a single discussion board channel (discussionboard_channels table).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the channel to retrieve

responseBody.description: Full channel details as stored in the database.

operations.specification: Create a new discussion board channel. Associated with the 'discussionboard_channels' table in Prisma.
operations.description: This operation allows creation of a new top-level channel grouping for the discussion board platform. It validates the uniqueness of the channel name, description, and initial visibility status. User must have admin privileges. The request payload follows the IDiscussionboardChannel.ICreate structure with all necessary channel fields. On success, returns the new channel record. Validation errors may arise from duplicate names, missing required properties, or insufficient privileges.
operations.summary: Create a new discussion board channel (discussionboard_channels table).

requestBody.description: New channel data for creation.

responseBody.description: Created channel entity with full details.

operations.specification: Update an existing discussion board channel by id. Tied to the 'discussionboard_channels' table in the database.
operations.description: This endpoint allows updating metadata or visibility of a single channel (name, description, visible status, etc). Identified by path UUID. The update payload follows IDiscussionboardChannel.IUpdate. Successful requests return full updated entity. Permission enforced so only admins can update channels. Errors are returned for not found, duplicate names, validation, or permission issues.
operations.summary: Update a discussion board channel by id (discussionboard_channels table).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of the channel to update

requestBody.description: Fields to update for the channel (name, description, etc).

responseBody.description: Updated channel with all properties.

operations.specification: Delete (soft-delete) a discussion board channel by unique id. Linked to 'discussionboard_channels' database table.
operations.description: This endpoint marks a discussion board channel as deleted (soft delete), hiding it from general access while maintaining audit trail. The id path parameter is the UUID of the channel. Only admins can perform deletions per policy requirements. On success, returns confirmation or (optionally) deleted entity info. Returns errors for missing id, insufficient privileges, or already deleted channels.
operations.summary: Soft-delete a channel by id (discussionboard_channels table).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of the channel to delete.

responseBody.description: Operation outcome or the deleted channel entity.

operations.specification: Paginated and filtered listing of sections within discussion board channels, mapped to 'discussionboard_sections' table in Prisma.
operations.description: This endpoint retrieves sections associated with channels, supporting pagination, search by name/description, filtering by channel, and sorted ordering by position or date. It enables fine-grained lookup for both admin and user-facing board navigation. Results may be filtered by visibility or section activity status. Used in UI navigation, admin dashboards, and section managers.
operations.summary: List and search all board sections (discussionboard_sections table).

requestBody.description: Section list query filters and pagination options.

responseBody.description: Paginated section summaries.

operations.specification: Get a specific section of a channel by unique id, referencing 'discussionboard_sections' table.
operations.description: Fetches complete information about a section given its database UUID. Returns name, channel relationship, ordering, and all metadata fields per schema. Used for detailed section view or admin editing. Permission policies may restrict access to hidden/soft-deleted sections for some roles. Path parameter 'id' is always required and validated as UUID.
operations.summary: Get full details for a board section (discussionboard_sections table).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of the section to retrieve.

responseBody.description: Complete details about the board section.

operations.specification: Create a new section within a discussion board channel. Backed by the 'discussionboard_sections' Prisma table.
operations.description: Initiates a new section within a selected channel, specifying name, description, position, and visibility. Only admins can create sections. Request payload follows IDiscussionboardSection.ICreate. Validation includes unique name per channel, required fields, and admin role. On success, returns created section data. Errors for missing or invalid parameters, permission denied, or business violations (e.g., duplicate section).
operations.summary: Create a board section (discussionboard_sections table).

requestBody.description: Data for new section creation.

responseBody.description: Created section with details.

operations.specification: Update an existing section's data, given by UUID. Maps to 'discussionboard_sections' Prisma schema.
operations.description: Allows changes to section name, description, position, or visibility. Payload is validated and only admins may update. Returns the full, updated entity. Errors on not found, permission, or conflicting names/positions. Used in section management interfaces by admins.
operations.summary: Update a board section's information (discussionboard_sections table).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of the section to update.

requestBody.description: Section update information (name, position, etc).

responseBody.description: Updated section with all properties.

operations.specification: Delete (soft-delete) a section in a discussion channel by its id. Backs onto 'discussionboard_sections' Prisma table.
operations.description: Marks a section as deleted (soft delete, not removed from database). Requires admin rights. Deleted sections are hidden in UI but retained for audit. Errors returned when not found or permission denied. Path parameter is UUID section id.
operations.summary: Soft-delete a section by id (discussionboard_sections table).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of the section to delete.

responseBody.description: Deleted section or operation outcome.

operations.specification: Query, search and list all system configuration records for the discussion board. Uses the 'discussionboard_configurations' Prisma table.
operations.description: This API provides a multi-parameter search/filter interface for configurations system-wide, with paginated results. Supports filtering by key, value type, description, or creation/update timestamps. Used by admins for reviewing/changing platform-wide behavior. All fields per IDiscussionboardConfiguration.ISummary model. Permission rules may restrict some sensitive config keys. Errors for improper filters, permission fails, or query issues.
operations.summary: Paginated listing and search of system configuration records (discussionboard_configurations table).

requestBody.description: Configuration list filtering, sorting, paging criteria.

responseBody.description: Paginated summary list of configurations.

operations.specification: Get full details of a single system configuration by its unique id. Uses the discussionboard_configurations table.
operations.description: Retrieves all fields of a single configuration entry, for audit, changing or documentation. Path parameter is UUID of the config row. Restricted to admin users. Used by configuration UI, audit panels, or automated deployment scripts. Errors for bad id or missing permission.
operations.summary: Get details of a single configuration record (discussionboard_configurations table).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of the configuration record to retrieve.

responseBody.description: Complete configuration record with all properties.

operations.specification: Create a new system configuration entry in discussionboard_configurations. This operation allows authorized administrators to add a new platform-wide configuration parameter for the discussion board application, such as toggling maintenance mode, configuring global limits, or changing policy strings. The payload specifies the atomic config_key, config_value (as string), value_type (such as boolean/int/string/datetime), and optional description. Creation and update timestamps are managed automatically. All configuration parameters must be unique by config_key and are strictly enforced at the database level. This endpoint is essential for DevOps and admin panel integration to handle runtime and policy settings. Only platform administrators are authorized to perform this operation.
operations.description: This operation creates a new system configuration entry in discussionboard_configurations. The body must include config_key (string), config_value (string), value_type (string, like 'boolean'/'int'/'string'/'datetime'), and an optional description. Upon creation, system-managed timestamps are recorded. Only admins may invoke this endpoint. Attempts to duplicate config_key will result in an error; config keys are unique and required for mapping application configuration at runtime. All system, security, and audit logging for configuration events should be consulted in tandem for compliance. Authorization token is required.
operations.summary: Create a new configuration in discussionboard_configurations.

requestBody.description: Configuration creation details. Must include: config_key, config_value, value_type, and optional description.

responseBody.description: The created configuration entry details in the system.

operations.specification: Update an existing configuration entry identified by its UUID in discussionboard_configurations. This enables modification of system-wide operational or policy configuration parameters, adhering to platform audit and compliance requirements. Configuration modifications require strict validation: only the config_value, value_type, and description can be updated. The config_key and id are immutable; creation timestamp never changes, but updated_at is set to the time of modification. The endpoint enforces unique constraints and proper atomicity of configuration parameters. Only platform administrators have modify permission. Use for admin UI configuration change features and runtime system tuning.
operations.description: This operation updates an existing configuration in discussionboard_configurations by UUID. Accepts input for config_value, value_type, and description; config_key and id are immutable and cannot be changed. Authorization is required and only admins are permitted access. Attempts to update non-existent configurations will return a 404 error. Audit log entries should record the update. Unique constraints are validated on the config_key, and all updates record updated_at timestamp for compliance.
operations.summary: Update an existing configuration in discussionboard_configurations.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Target configuration's UUID.

requestBody.description: Config update information: value, type, description (cannot update id or config_key).

responseBody.description: The updated configuration entry.

operations.specification: Remove a configuration entry (soft-delete) from discussionboard_configurations by UUID. This operation marks the configuration as deleted for compliance and audit; actual record remains for historical reference. Only system administrators have the authority to delete configurations. Invoking this endpoint updates the record's soft-delete field (not a hard delete), allowing potential restoration and complete audit trails for past system settings. Used in admin UIs and DevOps workflows when a configuration becomes obsolete or policy changes.
operations.description: This endpoint marks a configuration in discussionboard_configurations as deleted (soft-deletion) using its UUID. Soft-deletion ensures the database retains the record for compliance and auditing but removes it from active configuration loads. Authorization is restricted to system admins. If the ID does not exist, a 404 error is returned. All deletions must be logged in the system audit log. Attempts to delete a configuration that is already deleted will have no side effect beyond idempotent compliance logging.
operations.summary: Soft-delete a configuration in discussionboard_configurations.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Target configuration's UUID to delete.

responseBody.description: No content. Indicates soft-deletion was successful or already completed.

operations.specification: Retrieve a paginated, searchable list of audit logs from discussionboard_audit_logs for compliance reviews. This endpoint is crucial for administrators to monitor and inspect policy-critical or sensitive actions throughout the system (e.g., configuration changes, moderation actions, user escalation events). Supports search/filtering by actor_id, action_type, action_scope, target_id, and timestamp ranges. The PATCH method allows a complex request body for filtering instead of relying on query parameters, supporting advanced search cases. All returned data is read-only and for review/reporting purposes—no sensitive information is redacted for authorized roles. Authorization: admin only.
operations.description: Returns a paginated, filtered list of audit log entries from discussionboard_audit_logs. Accepts advanced search criteria including actor_id, action_type, action_scope, target_id, and time range. Useful for compliance and post-incident analysis. Result includes metadata required for pagination and auditing. Access limited to admins; audit logs are read-only and retained permanently for regulatory compliance.
operations.summary: Retrieve/search audit logs from discussionboard_audit_logs (paginated/filterable).

requestBody.description: Search and filter options for retrieving audit logs; includes actor_id, action_type, time ranges, and pagination.

responseBody.description: A page of audit log entries, with pagination and summary metadata.

operations.specification: Retrieve the full details of a specific audit log entry from discussionboard_audit_logs by UUID. This endpoint enables administrators to fetch action metadata, actor relationships, and full compliance/audit context for a single logged event. Used during forensic reviews, post-incident analyses, or transparency reporting. All associated business object references are provided for context—real entity records may need to be queried separately. Authorization restricted to admins and platform compliance auditors.
operations.description: Gets a single audit log entry from discussionboard_audit_logs by its UUID. Full record of the action, actor, target, scope, and all metadata is included. The endpoint ensures all compliance/audit logging data can be promptly reviewed by authorized personnel only. If entry is not found, returns 404. Data never includes sensitive user details (such as plaintext passwords) but references to object UUIDs for cross-entity tracing.
operations.summary: Get a single audit log entry by ID from discussionboard_audit_logs.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of the audit log entry to retrieve.

responseBody.description: Complete audit log record for the given UUID.

operations.specification: Create a new audit log record in discussionboard_audit_logs. Used by system and administrative features for recording policy or configuration events, moderator/admin actions, or other critical workflow steps. Can be invoked by system internal code or admin panel for compliance/investigation. Input includes action_type, action_scope, actor_id (optional), target_id (optional), and metadata (optional). Automatic recording of creation timestamp is enforced. All insertions are permanently retained for legal and audit purposes. Only system admins can create manual audit records; most entries are system-generated.
operations.description: Adds an audit log entry to discussionboard_audit_logs. Requires the action_type (string), action_scope (string), optional actor_id/target_id (UUID), and metadata (string/JSON). creation timestamp is handled automatically. Only admins can manually invoke this endpoint, though most entries are created automatically by backend logic. Duplicate entries (by id) are not permitted; all actions are strictly auditable. Failure to supply valid action_type or action_scope returns 400 error; unauthorized access returns 403.
operations.summary: Create a new audit log entry in discussionboard_audit_logs.

requestBody.description: Audit log entry creation payload: action_type, action_scope, (optionally actor_id, target_id, metadata).

responseBody.description: Full details of created audit log entry.

operations.specification: Update an existing audit log record by UUID in discussionboard_audit_logs. Used for appending or correcting metadata (e.g., additional context after incident review). Only metadata and possibly references to target_id or actor_id can be updated; action_type and action_scope are immutable after initial creation. Full audit of all edit timestamps is preserved. Only admins can update logs, and only for legitimate post-incident reviews or compliance actions. Attempts to modify non-existent or restricted fields are rejected.
operations.description: This operation updates certain fields (metadata, actor_id, target_id) for an existing audit log entry in discussionboard_audit_logs by UUID. Audit logs are fundamentally immutable for core data, but metadata/context or associations may be corrected for audit purposes. Returns updated record or 404 if not found. Strict authorization applies and all edits are themselves logged for meta-audit. Attempts to tamper with action_type, action_scope, or creation times result in 403/400 errors. Used almost exclusively for compliance adjustments.
operations.summary: Update selected audit log entry details in discussionboard_audit_logs.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of the audit log entry to update.

requestBody.description: Fields to update for the audit log entry (typically metadata, actor_id, target_id; action_type/action_scope immutable).

responseBody.description: Updated audit log record.

operations.specification: Soft-delete (mark as deleted) an audit log entry from discussionboard_audit_logs by its UUID. Used only in rare cases of administrative removal/expungement for regulatory or privacy compliance, since logs are typically permanent. Actual data is not removed—an expunged/deleted marker is set. Only platform administrators with elevated privileges control this endpoint, and every deletion is recorded in the meta-audit trails. This endpoint does not allow hard deletes and may be restricted by platform policy or system configuration.
operations.description: Soft-deletes (marks as deleted/expunged) a single audit log entry in discussionboard_audit_logs by its UUID. No record is actually erased; instead, the audit log entry is flagged for compliance. Only admins with special rights can invoke this. Used under GDPR/right-to-be-forgotten or similar mandates when platform policy requires log expungement for specific users/actions. Returns 204 No Content on success or 404 if not found or already deleted.
operations.summary: Soft-delete/expunge an audit log entry in discussionboard_audit_logs.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of the audit log entry to expunge.

responseBody.description: No content, indicates soft-delete completed or unnecessary.

operations.specification: Retrieve a paginated, searchable list of discussionboard_settings entries. This endpoint is used to fetch all global or scoped board settings, such as default sort order, notification toggles, or theme choices. Supports flexible filtering by section_id, owner_type, owner_id, and setting_key for admin review, audit, and user-facing settings configuration. PATCH is used for complex search and filtering logic, enabling advanced forms and UIs. Only authorized users (admins) can perform full-system listing; scoped listing may be available for section or member owners.
operations.description: Returns a filtered, paginated list of discussionboard_settings entries. Supports filtering on section, owner, setting key, creation/update date, and returns relevant metadata for pagination in result set. Primarily used by administrators to review/edit platform settings, with further scoping for section/member possible. Returns metadata and summary for UI and audit. Access control restricts visibility per role and scope.
operations.summary: Retrieve/search discussionboard_settings (paginated/filterable).

requestBody.description: Filtering, search, and pagination options for settings list.

responseBody.description: A page of settings entries, with pagination and summary metadata.

operations.specification: Get the details of a single settings entry from discussionboard_settings by its UUID. Used to fetch a specific platform or section/member-scoped setting for review/edit by platform administrators. Staff may retrieve for audit or compliance checks. Entry is returned in its entirety—updates/edits should use the PUT endpoint. Only authorized admins or scoped owners may retrieve non-global entries. If setting does not exist, returns 404.
operations.description: Retrieves the full settings entry by UUID from discussionboard_settings. Returns atomic value of each property: setting_key, value, owner_type, and optional contextual notes. Only authorized staff or valid owners may access, with system-wide settings restricted to administrators. Used for admin UI, compliance reviews, and personalized settings display.
operations.summary: Get one settings entry from discussionboard_settings by ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of the settings entry to retrieve.

responseBody.description: The requested settings entry in detail.

operations.specification: Create a new global/section/member-scoped settings entry in discussionboard_settings. This allows addition of new configurable parameters tied to system, section, or user. Input includes setting_key, setting_value, owner_type (one of: global/section/member), and owner_id (nullable, required for section/member). Optionally, a reference to section (for section-owned setting) can be specified. Used by administrators to add new configuration possibilities or migrate legacy params to modern settings infra. Authorization: admin only for global/section, member for personal settings as permitted.
operations.description: Adds a new row to discussionboard_settings. Input must specify: setting_key (string), setting_value (string), owner_type ('global', 'section', or 'member'), and optional owner_id/section_id for scoping. Description and timestamps are managed by the system. Only administrators (and member for personal settings, when allowed) can access. Unique constraints prevent duplicate (key, owner, owner_id) assignments. Handles all compliance/audit requirements automatically.
operations.summary: Create a new settings entry in discussionboard_settings.

requestBody.description: Settings entry creation info. Specify: setting_key, setting_value, owner_type, and (as needed) owner_id or section_id.

responseBody.description: Details of the newly created settings entry.

operations.specification: Update an existing entry in discussionboard_settings by UUID. Used for revising setting_value, updating description, or changing scope owner (where permitted). Input may only update fields except for id and setting_key (these are immutable). System-managed timestamps reflect the update. Only admins or valid owners may change settings for their scope. If entry does not exist, reply 404; if update is unauthorized, reply 403. All changes are fully auditable.
operations.description: Modifies properties of a settings entry in discussionboard_settings, excluding id and setting_key (immutable). Editable fields include setting_value, owner_type, owner_id, description, and section_id. Last updated timestamp and change audit are managed by the system. Only authorized staff/owners may update settings in their scope.
operations.summary: Update a settings entry in discussionboard_settings by ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of the settings entry to update.

requestBody.description: Editable fields for the settings entry: value, owner info, description, etc.

responseBody.description: The updated settings entry details.

operations.specification: Implements the deletion of a specific settings record by unique ID. This operation is tied to the discussionboard_settings table, handling per-section, member, or global settings. The delete method performs a hard or soft deletion according to business policy, enforcing role-based authorization and providing audit logging. The endpoint is used for administrative or advanced member settings management, referencing all validations and constraints as documented in the schema and business logic. When a DELETE request is received at this endpoint, it will locate the settings record corresponding to the provided ID and perform the removal action, ensuring compliance with audit, traceability, and rollback requirements. Error handling is critical: non-existent or protected settings must trigger an appropriate error response, and audit logs should record the actor and action details. This endpoint forms part of the admin and section management suite, allowing fine-grained control over board behavior and user experience.
operations.description: This API operation deletes a global, per-section, or per-member settings entry from the discussionboard_settings table. The API requires a valid setting ID and will perform all necessary integrity checks to determine whether this setting can be safely deleted. If deletion is restricted (e.g., system-level settings or protected entries), it will return a policy error. All deletions are either soft (timestamped for recovery) or hard (permanent), according to platform retention policy. Upon successful deletion, the action is logged in the audit trail, noting the actor and change context for future compliance review. This API is used in admin and advanced user UIs for dynamic settings management, and is secured against unauthorized or accidental deletions, enforcing strict RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) based on the actor's authority (admin, section owner, or member).
operations.summary: Delete a specific discussionboard_settings entry by ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the settings record to delete.

operations.specification: Implements advanced listing and searching for members in the discussionboard_members table. Utilizes PATCH to allow complex query parameters (pagination, filters, sorts) in the request body. Permits admins and authorized users to search, filter, and review registered users, including activation, audit state, deletion status, and more. Includes support for RBAC filtering and compliance review as detailed in requirements. The endpoint supports search by username, email, status, and more advanced fields where required by policy. Designed for system and admin consoles for user management.
operations.description: Retrieves a filtered, paginated list of members based on query request parameters sent in the request body. The endpoint processes complex search and filter conditions—such as username, email, creation dates, or account status—and returns members who match, ordered as specified. Each member entry summarizes core profile and status fields as per the discussionboard_members schema. RBAC ensures the results are limited to actors permitted to view user records (e.g., only admins or self for sensitive fields). Designed for use in management interfaces, audit tools, or member consoles, and integrated with traceable audit logging for compliance.
operations.summary: List and search discussionboard_members entries with complex querying.

requestBody.description: Search and filter conditions for retrieving member records.

responseBody.description: Paginated results and summary info for members matching the search criteria.

operations.specification: Implements retrieval of a single specific member by their unique ID. Maps directly to the discussionboard_members table for direct record access. The returned object provides all profile, status, and audit fields as allowed by role and privacy policy. Supports RBAC: admins see all fields, members see limited self-view, and privacy is enforced on sensitive attributes. Designed as a canonical 'get by id' endpoint.
operations.description: Retrieves full details for a single member matching the specified ID. The endpoint checks permissions and ensures the requesting actor can view this information based on RBAC and privacy constraints. Returns the entire member record with all profile and account detail fields from the discussionboard_members schema, plus related profile info if allowed. Error handling includes 404 for not found, and 403 for forbidden access. Results are used in admin/member profile views and for system auditing.
operations.summary: Get detailed discussionboard_members entry by ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the member record to retrieve.

responseBody.description: Full member record with fields allowed by RBAC and privacy policy.

operations.specification: Handles creation of a new member in discussionboard_members, based on input payload with all required identity, security, and profile information. Incorporates validation for unique fields (email, username), password policy, and initial state. Upon success, creates core member record and optionally related profile record. Invokes audit logging as per requirements and sends confirmation or welcome notification. Used by sign-up flows both for invited and open registration, with all appropriate validation and onboarding rules applied.
operations.description: Creates a new member record and associated profile as needed, based on data supplied in the request body. The operation validates required fields (email, username, password), checks for uniqueness, and enforces platform policies such as minimum password strength and email format. Upon success, inserts member in discussionboard_members and, if applicable, associated objects (profile, notification preferences). Also triggers audit log event for compliance. Failure modes include validation error, duplicate email/username, or policy block for restricted registration. Used in registration UIs, admin creation panels, and onboarding automations.
operations.summary: Create a new discussionboard_members entry.

requestBody.description: Member registration and profile data for new user creation.

responseBody.description: The created member record, including ID and status fields.

operations.specification: Implements update of an existing member record in discussionboard_members. Performs RBAC, validation, and audit logging. Accepts an update payload describing new attribute values: username, email, password, or status fields as allowed. Triggers audit trail on any changes; may also update related profile or preferences if supported by business logic. Follows the requirements for full account management, supports both self-update (with RBAC enforcement) and admin-level changes. Ensures validation and restricted fields (e.g., username uniqueness, password policy) are enforced.
operations.description: Updates a member record matching the provided ID in the path, with new data in the request body. Handles all business and policy constraints: only authorized actors (self or admins) can update, changes are validated and recorded in audit logs. Supports partial updates, triggers appropriate notification/confirmation flows. This operation is core for account management, profile editing, and admin/user-control UI. Error modes include forbidden (RBAC), conflict (email/username), and validation errors. Audit and traceability are strictly enforced for all change operations, and side-effects (e.g., email confirmation) are coordinated as specified in business logic.
operations.summary: Update a discussionboard_members entry by ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the member record to update.

requestBody.description: Fields to update for the target member record.

responseBody.description: The updated member record with applied changes.

operations.specification: Handles deletion of a member in discussionboard_members, following all data retention, soft/hard delete, and audit requirements. Enforces RBAC: only permitted actors (admins or self, under certain conditions) can perform this action. Deletion logic supports either soft-deletion (timestamped for possible recovery) or hard-deletion, depending on business policies and platform configuration. Invokes compliance logging, notifies system if downstream data/processes must be invalidated. Used as part of account management and GDPR/CCPA flows.

operations.description:
Deletes (soft- or hard-) the specified Community Guideline from the discussionboard_community_guidelines table. Main use cases: removing obsolete guidelines, clearing draft policies, or complying with legal/data retention requests.

- Permission: Restricted to admins or moderators.
- Logs all delete actions with full actor context.
- Returns success status or error message if not permitted or record does not exist.
- Deletion strategy (soft vs hard) is determined by business policy and compliance needs.

Related: GET /discussionboard/communityGuidelines/{id} (retrieve), PUT /discussionboard/communityGuidelines/{id} (update).
operations.summary: Delete a Community Guideline from discussionboard_community_guidelines (soft or hard-delete, per policy).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of the Community Guideline to delete.

IDiscussionboardAuditLogs.description: Normalized record of an audit/compliance event in discussionboard_audit_logs, with referential links to actors/resources and JSON-serialized metadata for compliance review.

IPageIDiscussionboardMember.description:
member(회원) 리스트/셀렉션 형태의 페이지 결과 컨테이너.

IDiscussionboardModerator.ICreate.description: 새 Moderator 권한 부여(create) 요청 구조. 반드시 멤버+관리자 UUID 지정 필요.

IDiscussionboardModerator.IUpdate.description:
This type defines the structure for updating moderator assignments within the actors domain of the political/economic discussion board platform. It is based on the discussionboard_moderators table and is typically used to revoke or manage moderator privileges for a member.

Reference: Prisma schema discussionboard_moderators and the requirements on moderator role lifecycles.

IDiscussionboardAdmin.IRequest.description: Request/criteria type for listing/searching discussion board administrator accounts. Implements admin panel, audit, and compliance listing/search workflows. Reference: discussionboard_admins table in Prisma.

IPageIDiscussionboardAdmin.description:
Paginated result container type for returning admin (system administrator) query results. Standard pagination contract.

- pagination: metadata per current page, total results, total pages, etc.

IDiscussionboardAdmin.description:
Admin account/entity type for platform administrators. Reference: discussionboard_admins table in actors domain.

Properties include primary key, email, username, and audit timestamps.

IDiscussionboardAdmin.ICreate.description:
Input type for creating a new administrator on the discussion board platform. Captures email, username, and password as necessary for account creation and initial onboarding.

IDiscussionboardMemberProfile.IRequest.description:

IDiscussionboardMemberProfile.IUpdate.description:
Type for updating one or more editable member profile fields. All properties are optional/nullable (see schema for details).

IDiscussionboardMemberHistory.IRequest.description:

IPageIDiscussionboardMemberHistory.description:

IdiscussionboardMemberHistories.description:
Record of a single change to member profile, role, or account, implemented per audit/compliance requirements (alternate variant for legacy endpoint compatibility).

IdiscussionboardBoards.IRequest.description:

IdiscussionboardBoards.description: A single discussion board entity, as used in major groupings of threads. Includes atomic ID, display label, status, and timestamps for audit.

IdiscussionboardBoardTags.ICreate.description:

IDiscussionboardThreadSnapshot.IUpdate.description: Update payload for an existing thread snapshot version record. Enables corrections as allowed by audit, compliance, and business policy.

IDiscussionboardThreadFollow.IRequest.description:

IPageDiscussionboardThreadFollow.description:

IDiscussionboardThreadFollow.description:

Each property comes directly from the discussionboard_thread_follows Prisma table. Follows enable notification delivery, member engagement analytics, and personalization. IDiscussionboardThreadFollow.ICreate.description:
API contract type for creating a thread follow.

Directly used when a member opts to follow a thread for notifications. Properties match the atomic fields from discussionboard_thread_follows.

IDiscussionboardThreadFollow.IUpdate.description: API contract type for updating thread follow state (soft delete for unfollow, or restoring a previously deleted follow). Only the deleted_at timestamp is editable.

null.description: Represents no response body (HTTP 204 or similar), for operations that intentionally return nothing. Used for delete endpoints or no-content responses.

IDiscussionboardPost.IRequest.description:
Request structure for post listing/search.

Used for PATCH endpoints retrieving lists of posts with complex filters and pagination. Each property matches an indexable/searchable field in the discussionboard_posts Prisma table, following board requirements for search, moderation, compliance, and audit.

IPageDiscussionboardPost.description:
Paginated wrapper for lists of discussion posts.

Contains both the page metadata (needed for navigation/UI) and the main array of posts being bulk-listed.

IDiscussionboardPost.description:
Core normalized post entity from the discussionboard_posts schema.

Contains all atomic fields that represent a member's post within a thread. Each property directly represents a column in the table, referenced in audit, moderation, compliance, and API contracts.

IDiscussionboardPost.ICreate.description:
Request shape for composing/creating a discussion post.

Used by POST endpoints (board posting) to create a new post, enforcing all Prisma schema requirements. Each property directly correlates to the normalized post database record for creation.

IDiscussionboardPost.IUpdate.description: Update contract for posts, permitting modification of title/body, state transitions and soft delete/restore, but not changing post/thread/author.

IDiscussionboardPostEditHistory.IRequest.description: Search/filter contract for listing post edit histories. Used in audit UIs or change review screens.

IPageDiscussionboardPostEditHistory.description:
A paginated result set of discussion board post edit history records.

This type is used when listing or searching the full audit trail for post edits, as defined by the 'discussionboard_post_edit_histories' Prisma schema. It includes pagination details and an array of individual edit events. Each record represents a single atomic edit of a post, created by members, moderators, or admins as per the strict auditing and compliance requirements of the discussion board system. This schema enables UIs and audit tools to efficiently page through high-volume edit histories while retaining full context for each change.

IDiscussionboardPostEditHistory.description:
A full atomic record of a post edit event in the discussion board.

This type represents a normalized history entry for an edit to a post, as recorded in the discussionboard_post_edit_histories table. It aligns with requirements for strict compliance, auditability, and transparency by capturing all relevant details: which post was edited, who made the edit, what the previous values were, and the reason for the edit. Used for displaying edit history UIs, supporting moderation and dispute resolution workflows, and enabling compliant rollback/forensics on post content modifications.

IDiscussionboardPostEditHistory.ICreate.description:
The payload for creating a new post edit history entry. Matches the structure and compliance requirements of the 'discussionboard_post_edit_histories' Prisma model.

All required audit properties must be present, and nullable fields are for unchanged or unavailable prior values. This schema enables compliance with the platform's strict audit and transparency mandates.

IDiscussionboardPostEditHistory.IUpdate.description:
Payload for updating (patching) an existing post edit history record for audit correction or administrative revision.

Optional fields may be supplied to amend an event; only supplied properties are updated. Strict audit logging and policy apply to modification of history entries.

IDiscussionboardPostLike.IRequest.description:
Request contract for searching, filtering, and paging post like records from the discussionboard_post_likes table.

Includes criteria for filtering by post, member, creation time, and standard pagination. Enables moderation, analytics, and user engagement reporting as per audit and discovery requirements.

IPageDiscussionboardPostLike.description:
Paginated response type for listing or searching post like records in the discussion board API.

Includes pagination controls and a list of like event objects. Used by moderation and user engagement reporting workflows, per requirements mapped to the discussionboard_post_likes DBA schema.

Idiscussionboard_postLikes.description:
Atomic representation of a single post like record in the discussion board system.

Matches one (member, post) pair with the corresponding timestamp. Enforces denormalized like-per-user rules from the requirements documentation and the Prisma post like schema.

Idiscussionboard_postLikes.ICreate.description:
Payload for creation of a new post like record in the discussion board API.

Mandates post and member cross-reference as per database integrity and business rule documentation. Used in user interaction, engagement analytics, and content popularity calculation.

Idiscussionboard_postLikes.IUpdate.description:
Payload for updating (patch/correcting) a post like record in the discussionboard_post_likes table.

Idiscussionboard_postDislikes.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and paging contract for querying post dislike records from the discussionboard_post_dislikes table.

Supports various analytics, moderation, and member profile use cases in the business logic.

IPageIdiscussionboard_postDislikes.description:
Paginated response object for lists of post dislike records from the discussion board.

Includes pagination info and the array of dislike actions, supporting UI views, moderation analytics, and audit workflows per the requirements and Prisma schema.

Idiscussionboard_postDislikes.description:
Normalized, atomic representation of a dislike event from the discussionboard_post_dislikes table.

Each record denotes a single member's negative response to a post and is crucial for analytics, policy enforcement, and engagement features described in the requirements and business logic.

Idiscussionboard_postDislikes.ICreate.description:
Request body structure for creating a new post dislike. Maps to the business case of a user expressing a negative reaction on a post, with strict normalization of each dislike event. Request body for listing, searching, or filtering post report records in the moderation and content policy workflow. Supports pagination, searching by reporter, post, code, date/time windows, and resolved status. All properties correspond to columns in the discussionboard_post_reports schema.

Intended for moderation UI, audit dashboards, and member report review features.

IPageIdiscussionboard_postReports.description:
Paginated result for listing post reports in discussionboard_post_reports. Used by admin/moderator dashboards for moderation queue, history display, and analytics.

Idiscussionboard_postReports.description:
Atomic report event entity for a discussion board post, mapping precisely to the discussionboard_post_reports schema.
